utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon to everyone. Mr. Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Good afternoon to everyone in the courtroom. This is case number IT-04-84-T, the Prosecutor versus Ramush Haradinaj et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. The Chamber was informed that both parties would like to address the Chamber. Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I can do so very briefly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I simply wanted to raise the question of the witness who is provisionally due to testify on Thursday, Zoran Stijovic. The Prosecution served on the Defence late on Wednesday night a 92 ter witness statement with exhibits to follow on the Thursday. And I notified Mr. Re and Mr. Zahar directly that given the anticipated content of the statement, the Defence would wish to file a motion concerning the admissibility of significant portions of the testimony that is to be adduced particularly in the form of summaries of documents annexed to the witness statement and the annexes themselves. That motion is close to being finalised and will be filed today, but one consequence may be certain difficulties so far as dealing with the evidence of Mr. Stijovic in full on Thursday is concerned, because given the nature of the anticipated testimony and the extent to which it relies upon material to which objection is taken, this is a matter which, in our submission, as we have set out in detail in the motion, needs properly to be resolved before the witness testifies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Of course the Chamber cannot respond in any way before we have seen your submissions, but we were on notice already that the Chamber could expect a filing in relation to this witness. Now, in the beginning you -- I think you carefully avoided mentioning the name, perhaps because there's -- it was uncertain whether there would be any protective measures.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: No, in fact I did mention the name and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then -- you then did, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm told -- I've been informed that there is no application for protective measures with respect to this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There'll be no applications for --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: No. In respect of all four witnesses we have listed for this week, there are no applications for protective measures.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. That's good. Yes, then -- okay. Then we'll wait and then this evening look at these submissions. Any other matter by the Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: With regard to the same matter, we will be joining in the submissions and may -- may well be filing additional submissions and we will be filing those by tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: We will be taking the same position.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. Then Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I -- I appreciate it's not the test whether the Defence are objecting to parts of a statement or which parts, but I just notify the Trial Chamber if Mr. Stijovic, who is supposed to be arriving on Wednesday, doesn't testify on Thursday, we will probably not have any witnesses as of Thursday. Professor Lecomte is coming on Wednesday and is available, we have told, only on Wednesday, she's in the middle of a trial in Paris. So those are our plans and if Mr. Stijovic doesn't come, we will have a difficulty. We have tried to get a reserve witness --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: -- but we haven't been successful.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Of course we cannot anticipate on a situation still to a certain extent unknown to the Chamber, but we are on notice of that as well. Was there any other matter the Prosecution would like to raise? Not?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then is the Prosecution ready to call its next witness? I do understand your next witness to be Mr. Shaban Balaj. MR. DI FAZIO: That's correct. I anticipate his evidence will be a combination of evidence adduced under Rule 92 ter --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: -- and orally.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I was informed that you have prepared a 92 ter summary for the first 17 paragraphs of his statement. Are there any objections against the summary? Mr. Emnmerson is nodding no. Mr. Guy-Smith, Mr. Harvey, that's three times "no." Then, Madam Usher, could you please escort the witness into the courtroom. MR. DI FAZIO: Will I be reading it out into the transcript?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think if you read it when the witness is there -- MR. DI FAZIO: Sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- then he is also aware -- MR. DI FAZIO: Yes. Yes, I agree.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Balaj. Can you hear me in a language you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Balaj, before you give evidence in this court, the Rules of Procedure and Evidence require you to make a solemn declaration that you'll speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth. I'd like to invite you to make that solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth. I swear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Balaj. Please be seated. Mr. Balaj, you will be first -- you'll be first examined by counsel for the Prosecution. I do not know whether you were informed about the way this is done. Since you have given already a statement, part of this statement will be summarised and -- so you don't have to repeat that portion, but then other parts you'll be examined about and then you'll have to answer the questions. Mr. Di Fazio. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you. If Your Honours please, I'd propose to ask the witness to identify his statement, and once he's done that and I've sought its admission, then I propose to read the summary, if that's okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And then, of course, apart from seeking him to identify his statement, the obligatory questions related to it. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed. MR. DI FAZIO: I'd ask that the witness be shown on the screen his statement, and that is 65 ter 2067. And it should be the Albanian signed version. Examination by Mr. Di Fazio:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could we scroll down to the bottom, please. Mr. Balaj, would you look to the bottom of that particular page. Do you see your signature on the commencement page of that statement? Can you see --

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thanks. You can pull your chair in a little closer if you want and just speak up a little bit so we can hear you. And you'll be there for a little while, so just relax.

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could the witness be shown the next page, please, at the bottom again. Thank you. And same question, Mr. Balaj: Is that your signature at the bottom?

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And the next page, please, again at the bottom. Same question: Your signature?

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Again, please, with the next page. The same question: Is that your signature that appears at the bottom?

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And just the last -- if we could do this just one more time, please. Next page. And again, at the bottom, is your signature, or at least part of your signature, apparent?

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And is that a statement that you gave to officers of the -- of the Office of the Prosecutor on the 2nd and 8th of June --

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And does it contain material that you would provide evidence of here in this court if you were asked questions about that? Those topics, that material.

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: I will respond as much as I can.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. But my -- my question is simply this: The first 17 paragraphs of this statement deal with all sorts of topics, including trips to Albania to procure arms and so on. If you were asked questions about that topic, would you repeat what is contained in your statement up to that point, up to paragraph 17?

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: I will.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please, I seek to tender the statement into evidence under the Rule.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Any objections against? No objections. Then it is submitted into evidence. Just for my information, Mr. Di Fazio, we received a copy of a statement which just says "the 2nd of June, 2007" and one of the -- I see that this is a combined -- MR. DI FAZIO: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- version. MR. DI FAZIO: I think there's just simply an oversight. The one on the 2nd of June is in all respects almost completely identical to the one dated the 2nd and 8th of June. It had to be fine-tuned and some minor matters were adjusted in it. The one that you should have is the English translation which bears the "2nd and 8th of June."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: That is the final polished version, so to speak, of the statement that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I have it on my screen at this moment, the English translation. MR. DI FAZIO: So that's 2nd and 8th of June.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But there are no major differences, from what I understand. MR. DI FAZIO: No. No. It's just -- no, there -- I'm sure there are no differences at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No differences at all. MR. DI FAZIO: But nonetheless, just for the sake of safety, can we deal with the 2nd and 8th of June.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I've got it -- I've got that version now on my screen. So please proceed -- MR. DI FAZIO: I'll now --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But first of all admitted into evidence but not yet assigned an exhibit number. Mr. Registrar, that would be ...?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be P922.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Please proceed, Mr. Di Fazio. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you. If Your Honours please, I'll now read a summary - and it's only a summary - of the evidence that is contained in those portions of Mr. Balaj's witness statement that has just been introduced into evidence. Shaban Balaj joined the KLA in March 1998 in his village of Strellc. A village guard was established after hearing that Gllogjan had also organised such a guard. Following the establishment of the village guard, the witness and about 40 people from his village left to obtain weapons in Albania and met up with other groups also engaged in the same task. The witness and his group made it to - I don't know how to pronounce this, I think it's Tropoje - and purchased arms and then headed back to Kosovo with the weapons being transported on horseback. They returned to Kosovo and going via Upper Jasic or Jasic, Junik, Rracaj, and then Gllogjan. From Gllogjan, they travelled to Strellc as Serb forces were located on the main roads. Mr. Balaj was aware of other such trips to Albania to purchase weapons from the end of March and some of his fellow villagers went on such convoys, most of which passed through Gllogjan, as this was the safest route, although other more dangerous routes existed through Carabreg and Strellc. Around the 7th or 8th of May, 1998, Mr. Balaj escorted a large group of people on their way from Drenica to Albania to obtain weapons. He acted as a guide and assisted the group as far as Gllogjan. Convoys travelled at night because Serb forces were not active at night. Mr. Balaj speaks of the communications methods adopted by villages, and this consisted of the use of satellite phones. Mr. Balaj noted the positions of Serb forces. Checkpoints existed along the Peja-Gjakova road, including two such checkpoints near Upper Strellc. Another check-point along the same road was located near Prilep, with one or two hundred Serb paramilitary and police forces. Other Serb positions existed at other points along this road as well as in various villages, such as Ljubenic and Decane itself. Occasionally Serb forces would venture from the main road for short periods of time. Serb forces entered Ljubisa or Ljubisa, Prilep, Carabreg. In May, Vranoc and Baran were captured for a short period of time by Serb forces.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Please, a bit slower. MR. DI FAZIO: A bit slower. I'm sorry. However, between the end of March and mid-August 1998, Serb forces were generally restricted to locations along the Peja-Gjakova road, although they did hold positions at Suka Herec, Suka Radonicka, Suka Babaloq, and Suka Bites. Mr. Balaj first received a KLA uniform from Albania during a trip there in March 1998 and it featured camouflage patterning and KLA insignia. Letters or authorisation cards were issued by KLA commanders permitting travel within KLA areas. Such authorisation cards were required to allow a person to pass through KLA checkpoints -- through KLA checkpoints. Almost all villages north and west of Lake Radonjic had KLA checkpoints. New cards were required for each -- each new trip an individual undertook. That, if Your Honours please, is just a summary of the written portion of the evidence that -- of Mr. Balaj that was just tendered. Just one final matter on the statement before we turn to his oral evidence. Could the -- could we scroll back until we find paragraph 5 of the -- of the statement, please. In the Albanian version, paragraph 5.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Balaj, would you just have a look at that. Just have a look at paragraph 5. And perhaps we could make it big. Can you -- can you read it easily, paragraph 5? Can you see it there? Number 5.

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, I think you might want to make a change to the date there. It says that at the end of March a group of people went to -- went -- left your village to go to Albania. Now, do you want to change the date and give us a -- another -- another date? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What -- when did this expedition --

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. It happened at the end of April. It is a mistake there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So you want to correct that, and paragraph 5 should read "at the end of April," and then all of the events that you describe happened in that paragraph.

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: That's right. You're right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you. If Your Honours please, I've done with that particular witness -- particular statement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Mr. Balaj, could you tell me if these personal details are correct: In 1998, you were living in Lower Strellc; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As far as your own brothers and sisters are concerned, I think you had two sisters and two brothers; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: One of those sisters was named Sanije.

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: She was born, I believe, on the 5th of December, 1963, and that made her about 35 years old in 1998. Would that be --

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: Yes. Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in 1998, she was the owner of a -- and in 1998, she was the owner of a -- of a small travel agency in -- in Peja.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I see. Okay. And in 1998, was she living with you?

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And she was unmarried.

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: No, she wasn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Thanks. I want you to turn your mind, please, to events on the 11th of August, 1998.

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I withdraw that, and I apologise. I'll reformulate my question. I want to draw your attention to events on the 12th of August, 1998.

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: Shall I start?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, no, just wait for my question. On -- on that particular day, was your sister residing with you?

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did she -- did she go anywhere on that particular day?

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where was she intending to go and what was the reason for her travel?

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: She was intending to go to Peja.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What for? Why?

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: She wanted to buy a mobile phone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how did she commence her journey? How did she start to get there?

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: At 8.30 in the morning, Hamdija and Haziri came, my cousins. They came by car. Hamdija was on the wheel. And I asked them, "Where are you going." And they said to Rosulje. I said, "Can my sister come along with you up to Rosulje and pass through Gllogjan?" Because that was the safest road for females to use, because they -- otherwise they couldn't go to Peja. They said yes. I gave them 2.000 -- I gave my sister 2.700 Deutschmarks, because that was the price for a mobile phone. They set out on their journey. When it was 3.00 or 4.00, I think, in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Can I just ask you to pause there. I just want a few more details, please. Firstly, were -- were there any children traveling on the trip in addition to your sister and -- and your -- and your two cousins?

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: No. There was a cousin, about 18 years old. He was also going to Peje to see father, because his family lived in Peje. He was going to Rosulje but he had nothing to do with the others. He just was a passenger, let's say. And then from Rosulje, he would go to a friend of his family and then wait for the bus that went to Peja. They went up to Baran. There was a check-point of KLA there, self-styled KLA, actually.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. Well, we'll ask you -- let me ask you the questions about that. But just tell me this: After --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Di Fazio, I noticed that the French translation is a couple of lines behind. So if you would please slow down a bit so that everyone has time to -- MR. DI FAZIO: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- transcribe and to translate. MR. DI FAZIO: Certainly, Your Honours. I apologise for -- yes, I apologise for my speed. There's just --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Also, if I might caution Mr. Di Fazio to make a distinction between that information which is from the personal knowledge of the witness and that information which is hearsay information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I take it that you take that on board, Mr. Di Fazio. MR. DI FAZIO: I certainly do.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Just one matter of clarification best with, I think, with the witness. Page 13, line 2 the route to be taken is recorded as "passed through Gllogjan?" I think the witness's testimony was Leshan rather than Gllogjan.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please seek clarification of that. MR. DI FAZIO: I will. In fact, I'll show him a map and ask him to -- at a later point to indicate some of these places but perhaps I'll just clarify that last point.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As far as you're aware, did your sister's intended route that morning on her way to collect her telephone -- buy her telephone, would that have taken her through Gllogjan or would she have avoided it?

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: No. No. The road didn't pass through Gllogjan but through Baran and to Rosulje then. There is Leshan village where the bus stopped, because the bus didn't go to Rosulje but to Leshan village. That was where the bus that went to Peje stopped.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And just one more question about your sister. Was she ever a member of the KLA as far as you were aware?

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: She was to buy foodstuffs for the families that I kept in my own home in Malisheve. She was wearing a uniform but it was a uniform I gave her and she was carrying a rifle that I gave her. She was there to purchase some foodstuffs. She met some girls who were singing the Albanian hymn and hoisting the flag. She sang a couple of songs with them and she lined up with them. That was as far as her KLA, let's say, participation lasted.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you for explaining that. And on this particular day that she left in the car to go off and buy the telephone, was she dressed in KLA uniform or was she dressed in civilian clothes?

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: No. She was wearing normal dress and she was wearing sandals and carrying a bag.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Following her departure with these -- with your cousins, in the car, did you ever see your sister alive again?

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: Never. Only on the day that I received her dead body from the morgue.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Okay. Now, you -- earlier you started to tell us that you learnt of certain matters that day. Could you now tell Trial Chamber if -- if you saw your cousins again, the men that she'd left with that morning, and where and when you saw them and under what circumstances.

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: Haziri came back. In Baran they were stopped. Commander Mete Krasniqi, he was self-styled commander of the KLA.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can I just ask you -- can I just interrupt you there. I'm going to ask you to give details about what your cousins told you. But we want to be clear -- the Trial Chamber wants to be clear and all the lawyers want to know how you know things. And at this stage, I'm just asking you to tell -- tell the Trial Chamber what your cousins said to you when you saw them again that day. Just report to the Trial Chamber what they told you when you first saw them again.

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: My cousins went up to Rosulje, returned to Baran, and asked for my sister. And they were told that she went to Strellc, to her village. They came back from Baran and came up to me. It was about 3.30 or 4.00, I think, 2.30. I can't be very precise. And they recount -- they asked me, "Is Sanije back?" I said, "No." And I said, "What happened?" And they said, "That Mete Krasniqi came out and stopped us," them, that is. There was Vesel Dizdari with him, Avni Krasniqi, Iber Krasniqi and this person who killed her, his pseudonym was Galani. At that time, I didn't know him. His name is Idriz Gashi. I talked with them and I took my car, took my rifle.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Just pause there. Now, this information that you've just given us - okay, that -- that she'd been stopped and amongst the persons who stopped her were all of these gentlemen, Ahmet Krasniqi, Iber Krasniqi, and so on. Were you actually told, actually given those names, actually told that by your cousins when they returned or is this something you've learnt later?

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: No. They told me -- they showed me the persons who stopped-- persons who stopped them. I dressed, got my car and my rifle, and together with Hamdi and Hazir we went to Baran.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I just want to be clear about one name. I may have misled you, I suspect. But I think you mentioned Mete Krasniqi, not Ahmet Krasniqi; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: That's correct, Mete Krasniqi.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Thanks. Okay. All right. Well, now, you told us that you started to -- to do things. Tell us how you -- what you decided to do, how you approached this -- this business when you -- when your cousins returned. What did you do?

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: I was very understand -- understand -- upset, indeed, because I didn't owe them anything. And I set out very sad and angry at the same time. I wanted to meet them. We went to the red school that was Shkolle e Kuqe in Albanian, where the military police were located.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just pause there. Just pause there. Who were you in company with?

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: I was with Hamdi and Hazir, my cousins.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the school that you went to, which village is that located in?

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: In Baran.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, think carefully about this question: On the way to Baran, did you stop anywhere?

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: I stopped at Gani Gjukaj's to ask him go.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, just explain to the Trial Chamber who Gani Gjukaj is and why you stopped there. Just explain to the Trial Chamber why you stopped at his house, what you did there.

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: Gani Gjukaj was a commander of the village. He was a very sincere person. I stopped at his house to ask him -- I forgot to mention that on the 11th of August I went to him and took the authorisation, an official authorisation, for my sister to travel up to Rosulje because I didn't want her to go to the Serb-controlled territory but to Rosulje which was controlled by the KLA. I stopped and asked Gani, "Do you know anything about what happened?" He said, "No." And then I continued my way towards Baran. When I arrived in Baran, I went to the Shkolle e Kuqe it was called, meaning red school. Now it is white-washed. It is white. I entered the school, I didn't find anyone there, and turned to go towards Vranoc to meet Mete Krasniqi. On the way to Vranoc Hazir told me here is Mete with the white van.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Could I just ask you to pause there. You said that you went -- you continued -- you went to Vranoc.

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: Yes. We set out for Vranoc.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. And you went there to meet Mete Krasniqi -- Mete Krasniqi. What --

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: We set out to go to Vranoc but we met him at the entrance to Vranoc. There is a gas station there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I suppose my question is this: What was your plan before you met Mete Krasniqi? What had you intended to do by going to Vranoc? What was in your mind?

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: I wanted to ask him where my sister was and in the first place why they had stopped her.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So you were specifically looking, do I understand, for this gentleman Mete Krasniqi?

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: Because this is what my cousins told me. They told me that he was the main person among those persons who had stopped them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Well, you met him in the white -- in -- you met him in a white van. Can you tell the Trial Chamber what happened upon your encounter with him.

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: I blocked his road with my car. I came out of the car together with Hamdi and Hazir. He was with another person whom I didn't know. I don't know even now. I don't know who he was and I don't know his name. I opened the door of his van and told him to come out and asked him where my sister was. He answered and told me that they took her to Gllogjan. I said, "Why?" He said, "Because -- we stopped her and they took her to Gllogjan." I said to him, "If my sister does not come from Gllogjan, you will pay with your own life." I shut his door, he didn't say a word, and went on his way. I returned. When I set out for Gllogjan, I knew -- I knew -- I felt that it was a lie that Mete Krasniqi told me, but there was nothing I could do, because in Gllogjan people are not taken, are not killed. He just said that to lie to me. I, as I had set out to Gllogjan, when I was half in the -- halfway, there was an -- a lot of fighting going on. I tried to enter Gllogjan, but I couldn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can I just ask you to pause there for a moment. Is there a village in your area called Zllapek?

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: Yes. I forgot about it. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I just want to know, when the -- did you go to this village on this day you're telling us about or not?

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: Yes, we did go to Zllapek. We called Vesel Dizdari, we spoke with him. And he said, "Follow this issue because Mete and his brothers are very dangerous and especially that person called Galan." I did not know him, this person. We continued. I left Hamdi in Strellc and with Hazir we went to Gllogjan. As we went towards Gllogjan, there was a lot of fighting going on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thanks. I still want to get some more details please about this encounter in Zllapek. I haven't finished with that. You spoke to Vesel Dizdari.

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And he said follow this issue because Mete and his brothers are dangerous. Were any names mentioned other than Mete?

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were any names mentioned other than Mete Krasniqi's name?

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: Well, these were known, these people. Avni, Iber -- people knew that they were a group and that person called Galani, that everybody knows about him today. However, at that time nobody knew his name until the year 2000, 2001. I did not know his real name. That was Idriz Gashi. I only knew him as Galani, Commander Galani of Lugu.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thanks. And that shows why we have to be careful about being precise; all right? Because what I'd like to know is this: On that day when you were standing there with Vesel Dizdari - not later - but on that day, on that very day, were any other names mentioned to you by anyone, actually spoken out loud, other that Mete Krasniqi? That's what I want to know. Not something you learnt later. But on that day, that very day.

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: On that day, I did not meet anybody else who mentioned their names. After that day, I learnt that there had been Cufe Krasniqi who had interrogated my sister. That evening I heard that he had been the one who had interrogated her, but not that day. At the time when I was going to Gllogjan, about Cufe Krasniqi, that he had interrogated her. It was either the same evening or the next day that I learned that Cufe Krasniqi had interrogated her.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Well, just tell us from whom did you learn that.

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: I don't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who told you? Who said -- who informed you that Cufe Krasniqi had interrogated her?

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: Vesel Dizdari. When I returned from Gllogjan. Because I went back to him. He told me that Cufe Krasniqi, deputy commander he was called, was the one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Well, let's just go back now to your very first visit to Zllapek when you first spoke to Vesel Dizdari. Just -- just --

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: It was about --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Just wait for my question. Just wait for it and I'll ask it. Did you explain about your concern for your sister to him? Just answer that for now.

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: Yes, I did. And he was looking at me and he did not come close to my car. He spoke to Hamdi and Hazir more, because he could see that I was very upset. He did not approach me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you've already told us that on this occasion that he mentioned Mete Krasniqi. Did he say anything to you about what Mete Krasniqi had -- what connection he had with your concern about your sister?

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: I don't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said you -- you explained to him your -- your worries about what had happened with your sister. Do I understand?

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did he explain to you or say anything to you about Mete Krasniqi? If so, what precisely did he say to you about him??

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: Who do you mean? Mete?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did Vesel Dizdari say to you about Mete?

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: Vesel Dizdari said that, "She has been stopped and please follow this."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he say anything about who stopped her?

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he provide you with any names of who stopped her?

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: She had been stopped by Mete Krasniqi. He was the first one to stop her. And my cousins told me that Mete Krasniqi was the first. My cousins knew Mete Krasniqi, Avni, Iber, while this other person, Galani, they didn't know him. There were other people there, about 30 or 40 or 50. I don't know how many. But they were not the ones to stop her. Only these that I mentioned had stopped her.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Okay. All right. So after Zllapek, where did you proceed from there and after speaking to Vesel Dizdari?

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: I went back home. My friends, my relatives had come because of all these -- this sadness that had befallen our family. Why should this happen to us? Because people had learned that she had been stopped and they were asking why and how. Friends from the KLA had come to my house. Neighbours, relatives. And I went to Gllogjan with Hazir. Hamdi did not come with us. He -- we -- he got off. But when we went close to Gllogjan, it was raining and there was fighting and we could not get in there. That's where we met a soldier from Gllogjan, coming from Gllogjan, and I turned the car. This soldier came in. His surname was Dervishaj. I don't know his first name. So we travelled to Gllogjan, and we went home.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Okay. Do I understand you that you didn't actually make it into the village of Gllogjan? Just answer me yes or no. You didn't actually get into Gllogjan because of the fighting.

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: No, we couldn't get in because there was fighting going on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thanks. Now, explain to the Trial Chamber why you went there in the first place. What was -- what was in your mind? What did you intend to do if you'd been able to get through?

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: I knew that this was a provocation on the part of Mete. But I wanted to know and I wanted to reveal his lie, because he lied to me. He lied. He betrayed and he was untruthful to me. I knew that there was nothing true in what he told me. I told Hamdi and Hazir after we left that he lied to us and he betrayed us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Well, that -- that might be what you thought. But how was going to Gllogjan going to help you? What exactly were you intending to do? Or to put the question another way: What would you have done if you'd been able to get into Gllogjan?

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: Well, I intended to go to my father's uncle's, because they lived in Gllogjan, Sejfijaj, is the surname, and asked them. And I intended to meet Ramush, because I knew that Mete Krasniqi had lied. I just wanted to uncover this lie. Because I had never heard about any wrongdoings occurring in Gllogjan. I thought I was betrayed. I was lost. He betrayed me. And that's why I wanted to go there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Is that Ramush Haradinaj?

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: Where do you mean?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that you wanted to -- intended to meet Ramush. My question is: Do you mean Ramush Haradinaj? Is it --

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. I wanted to meet him personally, because he was a very polite person. There was no problem in meeting him. I could have met him if I wanted --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I just want to understand. So you -- were you going to take your problem to him and enlist his aid, if possible?

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. All right. So you didn't make it into Gllogjan because of the fighting. And did you return home?

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: No, I couldn't get there, so I went back home.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Balaj, could I -- no, it's me speaking at this moment. Could I ask you not to seek eye contact at this moment with the accused. Would you please focus on Mr. Di Fazio, who's putting the questions to you, and could I also ask the accused not to in any way respond to eye contact either established by you or by the witness. Please proceed. MR. DI FAZIO: All right. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want you to start thinking now about the -- the events of the next day; that's the 13th. Did you continue your inquiries to try and locate your sister?

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: Yes, the next day, early in the morning, I continued -- I went to Lugu i Baranit, where she was executed. We asked people around whether they had seen her and I could get through to Cufe Krasniqi, but he was not there. The second day, I asked people again and I went to Tahir Zemaj in Prapacan. I explained him the case, what had happened.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just a minute. The next day -- this is the 13th you're talking about now. You said you went to Lugu i Baran. Did you actually go to Baran?

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: Yes. I went to Lugu i Baranit and to Tahir Zemaj the same day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Yeah, did you actually go to the village of Baran as well apart from going to Lugu i Baran?

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: I went there, but I couldn't meet any of the people who had stopped my sister. I saw the people. I saw other soldiers. I went inside. But I couldn't meet Mete. I couldn't meet Vesel. Neither Avni or Iber, although the latter I only knew him very little, by face. I saw people there but I didn't know them. I asked for Cufe Krasniqi, a soldier came out and he said that he didn't know where he was. I went to Tahir Zemaj. I told the story to him. He said that they would take measures. He must have undertaken his investigation as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, this is all -- this is all happening the next day. Do I understand you correctly? The -- the 13th, that's when you saw -- when you saw Tahir Zemaj.

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you've mentioned -- you've mentioned this gentleman Cufe Krasniqi in your evidence.

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see him at all that day?

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: The next day, on the 14th, I think it was. That's what -- that's when I met him. I went first in the morning. I couldn't see him. Then I went at about 2.00 or 3.00 p.m. He was inside. A soldier called him. Cufe came out. And he begged me --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Well, I'm going to ask you about Cufe Krasniqi later, but let's just go through it in chronological order. We're still now dealing with the 13th, the day after. You've told us that you went to Baran.

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You spoke to Tahir Zemaj and he said --

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And he said that they would take measures. Do you know what measures were taken?

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: Yes. Tahir Zemaj had called Mete Krasniqi, Avni Krasniqi, and Iber Krasniqi, Cufe Krasniqi as well, all of them and some other people whose names I don't know, and he had asked him questions -- them questions. But Idriz Gashi had left; he did not report to Tahir Zemaj to be questioned. So he did not go there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know a gentleman named Hysen or Hysan Gashi?

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know --

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: Hysen Gashi.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you for the pronunciation. Hysen Gashi. Do you know a gentleman named Fadil Nimani? Fadil Nimani?

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: Yes, I know that person. He was a very good man, a good strategist, and he came from a very good family.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see either of those two gentlemen in your searches for your sister or --

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. Yes, I met them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And how did you come to meet them?

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: Tahir Zemaj took me to them. When I went back for the second time, he introduced me to them and they started asking me questions about what happened to my sister. They were not in Tahir's barracks. They were situated in the clinic close to the road, close to the school where the barracks were located. I went into their office. They started to take notes. We started speaking about my sister. And for four or five days I went there and they asked me questions and I wanted information from them about my sister's fate.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Anyway, it was Tahir Zemaj who introduced you to them; do I understand you correctly?

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it was after he introduced you to them that they started this business of asking questions?

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: Yes. They started asking questions such as: Where was your sister intending to go? What did she want to buy? There was -- they were asking me how I felt, and please don't rush into things. Everything will be clear in -- and Fadil will clear up everything. So every day I went there from 2.00 p.m. in the evening or 8.00 in the morning till noon. Sometimes I went in the morning, sometimes in the evening -- in the afternoon. And I thanked them for the way they worked with me and -- for their work. The fourth or the fifth day I was waiting for them and they came in and Fadil Nimani said, "Well, my condolences, because your sister is dead." And then I lost consciousness. They gave me some water to drink. And I left.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. While we're on this specific topic, did they explain how she had met her death?

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: No. No. They just said that they had learnt that my sister had died and that they would investigate further into the case, try to find her body. I greeted them and left, because -- and I also thanked them because of the work they had done. I just pleaded with them for me to be able to get her body back, and they told me -- they told me that they would continue investigating. And that's how we parted.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you for that explanation. All right. Now, let's just -- we've gone ahead a few days. Now, let's go back now to the 13th. Okay? That's the day after you first learnt of your sister's disappearance. All right? Now, you've told us that on that day -- on that day you met Tahir Zemaj and that various things happened. You also said that you did not meet Cufe Krasniqi that day but the day after. So that takes us to the 14th. Correct?

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: Well, the 13th or the 14th. I'm not really sure. But either one of those dates --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: -- it could be the one that I met him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Fine. Fine. Fine. I understand. I'm not going to press you to it. That's understandable. Can you tell us this, at least: Would you say that you met Cufe Krasniqi on the same day that you met Tahir Zemaj or was it on the day after?

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: It could have been the same day or the day after. I can't remember exactly. It's been a long time. However, I met him -- as I told you, I asked for him at the gate of the barracks. A soldier went to get him. Cufe came out --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Slow it down. Slow it down, first of all. Firstly, where? What village did you -- where did you see him, Mr. Cufe Krasniqi?

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: In Baran, where the barracks were, the military barracks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thanks. Did you seek him out?

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was your purpose? Why him?

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: Well, I wanted to ask him about my sister, what happened to her and where she was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And did you actually succeed in having a meeting with him and speaking to him about this?

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: Yes. It was a very calm encounter. He -- we shook hands and he asked me who I was. I told him that I was Shaban Balaj from Strellc and that I had gone there to ask about my sister and what happened to her, because I was told that he had interrogated her. There was a little shop there, a coffee-shop. He told me we could go there and drink something. I said no. He said, "Let's go back into the barracks." I said, "No." I was unshaven. I had a Kalashnikov in my hand, but not to threaten him or anything. We got into my car, a red Lada [as interpreted], and he told me what had happened. He said that he had been in the office of Nazif Ramabaja; Avni Krasniqi and Iber Krasniqi had come and told him that they had captured a Serb collaborator, a -- a suspicious person and had asked him to interrogate her. He had gone there, greeted her. There were three of them there: Avni, Iber, and Galani. Avni and Iber had left the room, the office. He had asked her questions, where she was from. My sister had answered him. And I found," he said, "I found a name of a person" -- well, I'm not sure whether that was true. I think that that was a slander. Dragan Corovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can I just ask you, just pause there. You're doing well so far. All I want you to do now is not tell us what you think, what's true, what's slanderous, what isn't. Just tell us what came out of his mouth. Just tell us, tell the Trial Chamber what he told you as you're sitting in the car. Continue, please.

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: Well, he didn't say anything to this effect when we were in the car. He just said there was nothing about her and that he had released her. Even in the trial in Peja he did not mention this. However, even if she really had an address in her notebook, she had a travel agency. And when she had this agency, there were lots of Serbs living in Peje and they travelled, of course, as we did. He said that Galani stayed in the office all the time while she was interrogating Sanije, while Avni and Iber had gone out. When he had opened the bag that my sister had and found the 2.800 Deutschmarks in there, Galan was in the office. I don't know why that person was in the office while he was conducting this kind of job. However, he left. So he got out of the car, and I went on my way again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Okay. Now, you said that Mr. Cufe -- Cufe, sorry, Cufe Krasniqi had said, "I found a -- a name of a person. Well, I'm not sure whether that was true." He actually said those words to you? Is that what your -- is that your evidence?

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the name Dragan Corovic, was that the name -- did he actually mention that name to you as you were sitting in the car discussing this?

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: No, he didn't mention that name in the car. I heard it here. He didn't mention that even when he gave a statement to Peje court when the accused was condemned. MR. DI FAZIO: Could Your Honours just give me a moment.

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: MR. DI FAZIO: All right. Okay.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that you -- earlier in your evidence today that you had gone to Gllogjan in an attempt to get into the village and that part of your reasoning was that you had gone -- you had wanted to take your case to -- to Mr. -- Mr. Ramush Haradinaj. Did -- as far as you're aware, did Mr. Haradinaj respond in any way to your predicament?

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: I don't remember the date. I don't remember -- because I was very upset indeed. After three, four, or five days - I'm not sure - I went again to Gllogjan with Hazir. There was Taf Tafaj, an in-law of ours, who accompanied us up to Gllogjan in my car. He's got nothing to do with this affair. He was simply escorting us. He didn't know anything. We entered Gllogjan, met an old man there, greeted him, and asked him, "Do you have a prison here?" He smiled back at me and said, "There isn't any such prison." I said, "Yes, but someone, a traitor to the nation, did a treacherous thing to me." He smiled a little and then he offered me a cigarette. Tafaj was in the car. He didn't know what was going on between me and that old man, what we -- we talked. I said good-bye to this old man and went back to the car and then we headed to Strellc. After two or three days, Gani Gjukaj told me -- I wasn't at home. All the time I was searching for my sister. I wanted to find her even if she were dead. Gani Gjukaj said to me that -- my wife told me that Ramush and Gani Gjukaj had come to my house to pay condolences for my sister; meaning that he had got nothing to do with that. I knew even before that that Ramush wasn't -- wasn't meddling in that affair at all. He had nothing to do with that. He had no finger at all in that. And I mentioned that in all my statements. And I swore to tell the truth and not to say anything against innocent people. This is what my wife told me. And I thanked them in their absence. I was happy that, say, that a commander comes to pay condolences to my house. I have mentioned that I am repeating here that from 2001, when I started to give interviews in Prizren, to this day that Ramush Haradinaj has got nothing to do with the death of my sister.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Well, that's very clear, and thank you for explaining that. Let's move on now to another topic, please. And that's this: As part of your inquiries, did you ever go in company with other men to the house of Mete Krasniqi?

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: I went. I don't remember well when it was, but one of those days with 20 persons. Once I went to Mete Krasniqi and we were in four cars. We went to his house escorted by old people who know things better. Our chairman was Shaqir Gjonbalaj, a neighbour of mine. He was a sort of representative of our group. Avni was hiding. His brother came out and received us. It was a very tense situation. He offered coffee to some four or five people, old people. As I said, we were about 20 persons in that group. Shaqir Balaj, my cousin, asked for Din Krasniqi. Din came. We talked. He felt very bad about what had happened. He had heard that my sister was killed. We had some very distant family relationship to Krasniqi's family.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can I just ask you to pause there and clarify some of the things you've said so far. Firstly, what -- what was the whole reason for this big group of people to go there? What -- what was to be achieved?

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: It is the kanun of Lek Dukagjini for a group of people to go and talk things over before you take a kind of revenge for what happens. We have these guestrooms which we call oda, this is where people sit down and -- to talk with each other about such things.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I take it that the disappearance of your sister was central to this -- to this issue?

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: Yes. Of course, we were there to ask account for what happened, because that was one of the persons who stopped her and he should know where she was taken and what happened to her.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is Din Krasniqi related in any way to Mete Krasniqi?

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: Yes. They are first cousins.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Okay. Now, you -- you told us that you went there with a big group and Shaqir was your spokesperson. Tell me how matters unfolded.

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: We were there, as I said, with this large group, and we discussed with Din was Mete wasn't there. Avni was hiding. We didn't meet Iber. And our old man Shaqir Balaj told Din Krasniqi, "Tell Mete, because I am telling you that in 24 hours we want our daughter back, dead or alive. We want her to come -- to be brought to Strellc." The visit ended. We left the house and went -- on the way out, we ran into Mete by accident. We exchanged some strong words and then Zeqir Balaj told Mete Krasniqi, "Talk with Din Krasniqi. He will tell you what we are here for."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, did -- did Mete -- on this occasion, did Mete Krasniqi say anything to you about these events?

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: No. I didn't talk with him personally at that moment. After three or four days, Mete Krasniqi had taken this red Golf car which he used and had taken the Hoxha, the Muslim priest, of Vranoc village. My -- Ramadan Gashi, my cousin; Zeqir Gjoci from Kodradiqi, he was also my cousin and a friend, someone I knew; Xhavit Ukaj, again from Kodradiqi, and came to the room of Shaqir Balaj. All the cousins got together, along with friends and well-wishers, a group of about 50, 60 persons. And Mete Krasniqi began to speak about the case of my sister. He started by saying, "I came here with all these people to swear for what happened. I was wrong to stop her, but I have nothing to do with her death. I came here to swear to you all that I didn't commit this act." My brother, Avni is involved in this, in this deed, and a person called Colonel Galani from Lugu i Drinit. Shaqir Gjonbalaj asked him and said to him, "Mete, if you bring the body, we will see after the war as to what happened. If you don't bring her dead body, according to the Lek Dukagjini kanun, you have -- you owe us two lives." Mete said, "The body has been taken away from Lugu i Isufit, where she was buried." Then Shaqir Balaj, this old man said, "Where is the body? Who took the body away?" And he said, "Galan, using force, had ordered them to take out the body from there. A person called Zymer Hasanaj had seen what had happened. He had told them to remove the body from that territory." They had been forced to remove the body. Shaqir Gjonbalaj asked him again, "Who took away the body?" Mete said, "My brother and Iber Krasniqi, but they were forced to do that. And Togeri removed the body from Lugu i Isufit but we don't know where."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who's Togeri?

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: I don't know who Togeri was. I don't know. I wasn't interested to find out who he was. This is what he said. It was only later, after one or two years, that I found out who he was. I said who he is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you find out one or two years about Togeri?

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: After one year I heard.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you hear about Togeri after one year?

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: I heard that in 2002, when I was asked, some people in the court showed me some information about him. They said, "He killed your sister." I said, "No, Togeri didn't kill my sister." And that was all. When I heard the name, it was Idriz Balaj. It was in the court, when I heard that and I have mentioned that in my statement. He didn't kill my sister. He's got nothing to do with the killing of my sister. Mete Krasniqi, with his methods, with his betrayal, said that he took the dead body with his jeep and she was -- she disappeared. I didn't trust him. I don't trust him even now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just a second. Mete Krasniqi said he -- listen. "He took the dead body with his jeep." Who took the dead body with whose jeep? Who was he talking about, as far as you are aware?

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: They had a lot of jeeps. He said, "It was Togeri's jeep." But he said, "Idriz Gashi forced them to do that." Excuse me, by Galani, because at that time I didn't know who Idriz Gashi was. He ordered Avni and Iber to pull out -- to take out the body from there. I believe that Galani would have done that, but not that Togeri might have done that. But these people are still alive. They were 40 people -- there were about 40 people there in that room where Mete Krasniqi said such words, and there are also other people that he brought along with him, like hoxha, Ramadan Gashi, Xhavit Ukaj, people who are still alive today. But I didn't trust what he said. I trusted only when he mentioned Idriz Gashi. But not the other one. And that was it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Di Fazio. MR. DI FAZIO: I was just about to say I've got one small topic and then I've just about finished.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then we'll make you do that. Then we'll let you finish the examination-in-chief. That would be the last topic you would want to cover? MR. DI FAZIO: One more. Just one more brief topic. [Prosecution counsel confer]. MR. DI FAZIO: Actually, I would prefer, if Your Honours don't mind, for the break. It will enable me just to review the last portion of evidence and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then I'll first ask Madam Usher to escort the witness out until after the break. Mr. Balaj, we'll have a break until quarter past 4.00. Would you please follow Madam Usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'd like to address the Defence. A request has been filed for leave to amend the indictment, from what I understand, mainly on the basis of new DNA results. Could the Defence give an indication on how much time they'd need to respond to that request.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Would it be unreasonable to ask for seven days?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you could do it quicker. I mean, we are coming closer and closer to the -- to the end to the Prosecution's case.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It seems to be a rather technical matter. I'm not saying that technical matters do not require a lot of attention now and then.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And, of course, nothing is said about what the evidentiary situation would be once the indictment has been amended. We're just talking at this moment about --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. I'm -- I'm happy to work to whatever timetable the Trial Chamber imposes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. If I would suggest three days, would that be an acceptable ...? I'm also looking at you, Mr. Guy-Smith, and you, Mr. Harvey.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Four.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Four days. That would mean that we would receive the answer by close of business on Thursday. One -- Monday would then be one day.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Harvey, would that be acceptable for you as well?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: I can work with that, Judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then the Chamber expects a position, a response by the Defence, not later than Thursday COB.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: If we're in the position to give it any sooner, we will certainly do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That would be appreciated. We'll have a break until quarter past 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could the Defence give an estimate on how much time they will need approximately for cross.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I anticipate nothing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Perhaps as much as -- as a half an hour. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Harvey?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Nothing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Di Fazio, please proceed. MR. DI FAZIO: Thanks, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just a couple of topics remain that I'd like to deal with. You'd mentioned, I think -- let me withdraw that. Do you know of a place called Lugu i Isufit?

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's a location near Vranoc?

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: It is close to Lower Vranoc, because there are two Vranocs, the lower one and the upper one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever go there in connection with your searches for your sister?

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did you come to go there?

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: According to information I was given by people I knew who knew that place.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And why did you go there? What did you -- what did you expect to achieve or hope to achieve by going there?

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: Well, I thought that when Fadil Nimani offered me his condolences, I -- she must have hidden somewhere. So her body must have been hidden somewhere, in the forest or the mountain. I had friends who had followed the situation and according to their words, I went and found the place where she had been buried. I also found her blood -- her blood there. It was close to a well. There was also a stream 7 to 10 metres away. And this was in a corner, in a ravine. She had been buried there about 40 to 50 centimetres below the surface of the earth. It had been covered. The place had been covered, but I found the soil had been freshly dug. And I stayed there. My friends from the KLA, my relatives, my brothers were trying to protect me. They were all around. I contacted them. They -- and they asked me whether I found her. I said yes. And some of them came. Some of them cried. And we continued.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you ever go back to that location during the trial of Idriz Gashi?

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: I did, after people who asked me questions, Robert Dean and Irving Morris asked me. That's when I went and visited the place again, together with them. Before, I went with the UNMIK forces. So that the accused person who was accused of having committing this crime, a person who was an evil person, who had killed this woman just because of the money, to take the money away from her, and he tried to slander our family. And he couldn't. No one can slander our family, because we are a family originating from the Gervalla family. Everybody knows them in Kosova. My father is from the Sejfijaj family from Gllogjan. We have three martyrs in our family. And also the Dervishaj family, three sons of this family are martyrs, who gave their life for the freedom of Kosovo. And one of them was Ramush Haradinaj's soldier, a soldier. He was Kuqi, his nickname was Kuqi. They cannot throw mud on our name.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you for that. You've explained -- you've explained your position. Now, I just want to ask you a few more questions about your sister, general questions. She -- she -- to finish up. She was -- she was running a travel agency, I think, in Peje. And earlier today you said that was at least until 1997. Can -- can you remember when she stopped running her -- her travel agency?

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: Well, 1996, 1997? I'm not sure. The Serb forces began to loot everything. Even the agency. I had money to maintain her, because my brothers work in Germany and they brought money home for us. And whenever I had money, she had money as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: We -- at that time, we paid 10 Deutschmarks for one litre of gas.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. So after she stopped working in -- in the travel agency or couldn't -- in fact couldn't continue her -- her job, did you support her?

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: Yes, of course. I supported her. I would have supported her until I died.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thanks. And did she live at home with you under your protection?

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: Of course. She lived in my house. She had her own room. She loved my -- my children. She was my younger sister.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did she --

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: I loved her very much.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Did she look after your children in the -- in the weeks and months before her disappearance?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. -- Mr. Di Fazio -- Mr. Balaj --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] She did. All the time. I worked all day and she took care of my children. She bought them clothes. Of course the money was mine, but she took care of the children and the house. We were sister and brother. We had nothing to hide from each other and my money was her money and her money was my money. We were one family, one home. And I will always try to find out what happened to her until I die.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Balaj, I earlier asked you to address -- to look at Mr. Di Fazio or to the Chamber, not to seek any eye contact with any other persons in this courtroom. Could I remind you that that's what I asked you and what seems to be difficult for you to do. Please proceed. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, Your Honour. I apologise. Now I am calmer, but for nine years I had this anger inside me, and now after the 3rd of July, when I buried my sister, it was like a wedding to us, because I brought her home. I brought her to her mom and dad. So today I'm much calmer than I was then. I wouldn't have been able then to give you a statement or to testify. Now I am, and I don't want anyone who is innocent to be involved in this, because I don't want any slander to fall upon any other family. We are a sincere family, an honourable family, and I would not allow anyone to slander us. MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you for that and explaining that. But I just want to return to your sister in that period of time before she last disappeared. You said that she -- she was living at home under your protection. You said that she was looking after your children from time to time and that she would buy them gifts. Is that what she was doing in the weeks and months leading up to her disappearance?

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: Yes, exactly. She did things around the house. She helped my wife to do the housework, to prepare food. At that time, I had many people living in my house, and she took care of them as well. It was very difficult to find food and other things at that time. She was able to do. She went to Malisheve and brought food, to us and to the neighbours and other villagers, to the whole village. And the whole village was grateful to her.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And these donations --

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: She loved my children very much.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And did those domestic tasks occupy her up until her disappearance?

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: Yes. She did all these things until her disappearance. She wanted to have a mobile phone in order for her to be able to make some money. There were many people in the village and in other places who wanted to speak to people abroad, and that was how this all started. She asked me for the money. I gave her the money. And that was -- that went for the worse, because she was looted and for nine years her body could not be found.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you for that. MR. DI FAZIO: And if Your Honours please, I have no further questions of this witness; however, the witness is most anxious, and I -- I know this, having spoken to him, to show the Trial Chamber four photographs of his sister's funeral. And I wonder if the -- the Trial Chamber could view these particular photographs. They do show his sister's burial. It shouldn't take very long at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is there any objection by the Defence? We understand the request to be not of a primary evidentiary nature but, rather ... Then, Mr. Balaj, I do understand that you'd like to show us a few photographs. And I think they could be best perhaps placed on the ELMO so that we can see them. The Chamber will allow you to show us the photographs of the funeral of your sister. I also take it, then, that there's no need to assign numbers to it. It will be on the record -- on the video record of this proceedings. Could we have the assistance of the technicians to have the ELMO ready. I think there we are. If you'd briefly, one by one, explain to us what we see, Mr. Balaj.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is my son. He was eight years old -- sorry, he was five, and he's holding his aunt's photograph. He's crying. Close to him is my daughter reading a statement about her life. This is a co-villager of mine who read the petition written by the Strellc village inhabitants and also telegrams coming from the diaspora and friends from all countries in America or in Holland, where I worked for several years. This happened on the 3rd of July, 2007. Then also you can see other children and the wreaths.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Madam Usher, could you please put the next picture on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Here are my friends, relatives, and they are praying for my sister in her funeral.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The third photograph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Here you can see hundreds of people who took part in the funeral. People tried to -- evil people tried to slander my family, but they couldn't. They didn't manage to do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And finally the fourth photograph.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is where my sister is lying -- my dear sister is lying, between my father and my mother. That's where her grave is. Thank you for accepting to see the photographs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber understands that this is very emotional for you, and the Chamber was -- as you may have noticed, the parties did not object in any way, and the Chamber was glad to give you this opportunity. At the same time, I would like to ask you now to focus again on the questions that will be put to you by Defence counsel, Mr. Balaj. Mr. Emnmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I made it clear, Your Honour, that I didn't anticipate any questions, and that is the position. There is, though, the one matter about the transcript that I would like, if I may, just very briefly to put on the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Can the witness keep his earphones on?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm in Your Honour's hands.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then out of an abundance of caution I -- Could I ask you to take off your earphones for a second. Yes, to take them off. Mr. Emnmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Simply this: Your Honour first raised the issue of the witness seeking eye contact. I think at page 26 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- line 4, and I simply wanted, for the sake of the record, to record the observations from where I was sitting that coincided with the witness looking around the courtroom, because on page 25, line 2 he was asked a question by Mr. Di Fazio about why he was going to Gllogjan. And then at page 25, lines 7 to 13 he answered that question by reference to Ramush.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And then Mr. Di Fazio asked which Ramush --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, his exact question was: Is that Ramush Haradinaj? To which the witness replied, as looking around the courtroom, "Where do you mean?"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I'm -- I'm aware of that. And I'm also aware that at the same time Mr. Haradinaj made a gesture which --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Which was him, I think, identifying himself as the person to whom --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
