utterances.text: I do understand the context of it. The context is now clear. At the same time, you will understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm not -- I entirely understand the admonishment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And matters are clear by now. Could the witness put his earphones on again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Witness complies]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Balaj, questions will be put to you now by Mr. Guy-Smith, who is counsel for the -- Defence counsel for Mr. Balaj. Please proceed, Mr. Guy-Smith. Mr. Guy-Smith is over there.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Good afternoon, sir.

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. Good afternoon to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I -- I want to start with trying to get a bit of an understanding of some of the things that you've testified here today. And I -- I'd like to start with when you first learned that your sister had disappeared. That information came to you from your cousins; correct?

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: The information was given to me by two of my relatives: Hamdi and Hazir, who were with her. And they told me about it. And after that, I started to try to trace her, where my sister was.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I understand. When you spoke with your two relatives, Hamdi and Hazir, they told you --

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: My -- I spoke to them in the afternoon, 2.00 or 3.00 p.m. or 4.00. I don't know. I'm not sure. At that time, I wasn't paying attention to the time, of course. I lost it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I understand, and I wasn't asking you about the time. What I was asking more specifically was about the information that they gave you. And when you spoke to your two relatives, you were told that they had spoken with Mete Krasniqi, who had told them that your sister had gone to Strellc, which was a lie; right? And by that I mean that Mete Krasniqi had lied.

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. Mete Krasniqi had told them that she had left for Strellc. In fact, it was Cufe Krasniqi who had told them that. They had not met Mete but Cufe. They had gone there to ask who had been interrogating her, and they were told it was Cufe Krasniqi, and that's how they learnt that she had gone to Strellc. Well, now at this moment I'm not sure. Somebody had told them that she had gone to Strellc. I met them in Strellc close to my house. I was at -- at a cousin's house, and they told me that they felt very bad about what had happened and told me everything. And I asked them - I was angry - "Why? Why did you allow this to happen? Why didn't you stay there?" But this was in vain. And I opened the door of my car and told them to get in and went to Gani Gjukaj. After Gani Gjukaj, we went to Baran.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: If I might, if you could bear with me and listen to some of the questions that I ask, perhaps it might go a little quicker for you and a little easier. Okay?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Before we continue, could I ask the assistance of the technicians. The scrolling on my system is irregular. Very often it gets stuck. I earlier noticed one of my colleagues had the same problem. But we are not -- now it's running fine with him. It's not running fine with me. Please proceed, Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: May -- am I in the midst of making a test of the scroll for the moment to see whether it's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. If you -- if you go to the pause and then to the continue, you'll finally get it running again.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But it's not -- it's not perfect.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. Cufe Krasniqi is a relative of Mete Krasniqi's; correct?

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Avni Krasniqi is Mete Krasniqi's brother; true?

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Iber Krasniqi is another --

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: His cousin. Their cousin. Mete's cousin, Cufe's cousin, and Avni's cousin. But he's closer to Mete and Avni than to Cufe.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: When you first heard about your sister, you were very upset. And when you were testifying earlier, you said you were very upset "because I did not owe them anything." And I want to ask you a couple of questions about that. When you said to us here that you did not owe them anything, is what you meant that you had no debt to them and that's why you were somewhat surprised and upset, because there was no debt as between your family and their family at that time.

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: I had no -- I did not owe them any debt, neither in money or anything else. But they were a self-styled army under the command of nobody. Their aim was to slander people, to rob people.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And when you say that "they were a self-styled army under the command of nobody whose aim was to slander and to rob people," you are referring to Mete Krasniqi, Avni Krasniqi, and Iber Krasniqi; correct?

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: Well, that is clear, because Mete stopped them. Avni and Iber went to Cufe Krasniqi, who had interrogated her, and Idriz Gashi, whose nickname was Galani, was there. So there was a command that could not be called a command, because a commander, an officer who interrogates someone should not allow anybody to be in that room and listen to what is going on. The name now is known, Idriz Gashi, and he stayed all the time in that office. This also was said in the trial in Peje. And -- this is what he said: That Avni and Iber came in and went out all the time while Galani, Idriz Gashi, stayed there all the time and saw the money. And that's why the killing happened, the murder happened, because of the money.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Now, you've mentioned the name of Galani, who is also known as Idriz Gashi. And I'd like to ask you one -- a simple question for the moment, which is: Do you know what relationship Idriz Gashi has to the Tahiraj family?

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: I have not heard any -- of any Tahirajs. Just Krasniqis.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Now, there --

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: Galani was in their staff, in the headquarters. He was there for a short time, but he had been seen in Mete Krasniqi's staff, which was located in Mete Krasniqi's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I want to turn to the first time that members of your family went to Mete Krasniqi's home in an attempt to resolve this matter.

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: Well, we went to Mete and to Din, because it's the same family. They are first cousins. Mete was the one who first stopped my sister, and then the other ones had taken the matter into their hands. Mete had left when the others took her, and she had nothing to do with what happened next.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: My -- my question is this: At the time that you went to Mete's -- Mete's home with members of your family, according to, as I understood it - and correct me if I'm wrong - according to the kanun of Dukagjini, you went there to resolve the issue of your sister's disappearance; correct?

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: Correct. That's why we went there, to resolve my sister's issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And when you went there to resolve that issue, you went there with village and elders, because under the kanun that is the way such disputes are resolved; correct? You bring the village elders with you so that the determination can be made of what is the proper thing to do.

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: Yes. We were all of the same mind, my uncles, my cousins. We agreed that one person should represent all of us. One would speak; we, the others would simply listen. And this is what the kanun of Lek Dukagjini prescribes in such circumstances.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: During the first meeting where Avni was hiding and Mete was not present, there was no resolution between your family and the Krasniqi family over your sister, was there? The first meeting.

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: That's correct. We met Din Krasniqi, who is the first cousin of Mete, and we told him -- we informed him of what we had agreed, that this elder -- elderly people, Shaqir Gjonbalaj, was the one who would convey our opinion of Mete Krasniqi and he set the deadline of 24 hours, as the kanun says, for them to find the dead body of my sister, whom we knew for sure was dead.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And when you say "as the kanun says," what the kanun says in this regard is that Mete Krasniqi had a responsibility to bring either her back alive or dead within 24 hours; otherwise, he would incur a debt to your family; correct?

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: Correct. He was obliged to do that, because he knew what he -- his brother had done. He knew that he worked with Galani. He -- he himself worked with Galani with his brothers. They were military police. They were commanders. They referred to each other by the name of "commander."

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: The second time that the families met together when they were about, I believe you said, some 50 men in the oda, that is when the Imam came, the imam -- and that would be Imam Gashi; right?

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: No. He was Mullah Llukmani. Imam Mullah Llukmani. He was a hoxha from Drenice but served as a hoxha in Vranoc.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Right. And in one of the photos that you showed us, he was one of the men that was present at the funeral; right?

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: No. He was a hoxha from Gllogjan.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: When the imam came with Mete Krasniqi, during that meeting that was the second attempt to resolve the matter according to the kanun of Lek Dukagjini; right?

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct, because he wouldn't dare come alone. He had chosen the imam, he had taken my first cousin, Ramadan Gashi, and the other cousin of mine, Zeqir Gjoci from Kodradiqi and a friend of mine and a native villager from Kodradiqi, who was a friend. They were all together. And when you come with someone, no matter what feuds you may have, we are supposed to receive the guest in this case, whoever that may be.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And whatever happened during that second meeting, would it be fair to call that a trial where all of you met together and tried to resolve the issue of what had happened to your sister, to accord responsibility and for any debts that were owed to be paid? That was the attempt.

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: We were already there. We were in the oda, because there were police check-points -- two police check-points surrounding the village, 200 metres away. Mete Krasniqi came and we -- we got there. We are 31 households, we of the Balaj family. And we have elderly people in our midst, young people. Of course, the young people didn't dare open their mouth, because only one was supposed to be the spokesperson of the entire Balaj family. It was he who asked -- who started the conversation with Mete. He said, "Why have you come here," to Mete. Mete said, "I have come here to absolve myself of any guilt. I was guilt -- I was to blame only for stopping her, but I have no other thing to do with her disappearance."

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And Mete also said -- and Mete also said during that trial that he couldn't guarantee --

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: He said this in the presence of all the participants, in the presence of the imam, of Ramadan Gashi, Zeqir Gjoci and Xhavit Ukaj, he said that, "I personally swear to you all that I didn't do anything as far as her death is concerned. I cannot swear for my brother, because he is stained." And in fact this came true in the court, because he was there. He was all the time there until her last moment of life. And this was proven in the trial.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And so my question to you is: At that time, he said that he was not able to swear for her brother, Avni Krasniqi, nor was he able to swear for the responsibility of Idriz Gashi, also known as Galani. He was not willing to say that they were not responsible.

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: He said they were responsible.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I see.

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: He wanted to swear for himself.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: During that trial, you've told us that the elder said, "If you don't bring her dead body, you owe us two bodies." Correct?

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: Correct. This is what he said, in the name of all of us, both young and old, that you should bring the body dead or alive. Mete said, "I cannot bring her body, because it has been removed from the original burial place." And our elder asked him, "Where is she?" And he retorted, "I don't know." He said further on that Galani forced his brother and Iber Krasniqi to -- and he mentioned the name of Togeri at that moment, to remove the body from there. "I don't know," he said, "where they took her."

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I understand. And my question to you is: Once again, when that statement was made, that if her body was not returned or if she was not returned, that they would owe you two bodies. That, once again, is according to the law of the kanun; correct?

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: Yes. It was said. And this is how it was left. He couldn't return the body. The body was -- the person who killed her was found, and he is Idriz Gashi, pseudonym Galani, self-styled commander, under nobody's command, called himself "commander of Lugu i Drinit, and he's suffering his sentence in Peje.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Has that debt been paid, the debt of two bodies, under the kanun?

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: No, it hasn't been paid. Now the criminal has come out in the open. But earlier or later it will be paid; if not by her brothers, by the -- her -- her nephew and niece, who cry for her even now. A time will come when they will pay them back.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: As -- as you sit here today, do you know whether or not Mete Krasniqi is alive or dead?

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: I heard that he is dead.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: You contacted UNMIK in 1998 and spoke to them about the information that you had concerning --

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: I didn't meet anyone else there. In 1998? Not in -- in 1998, there wasn't any UNMIK.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I want to read something to you and see if this refreshes your recollection of meeting some people from UNMIK at the regional headquarters in Peja on the 28th of September -- I'm sorry, that was in 2002. My apologies.

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: In which you discussed the disappearance of your sister and the movement of her body. And this is what you told them.

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: "I state that on the 12th of August, 1998, my sister, called Sanije Balaj from Strellc i Uleti headed towards Peje"?

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: "On the above-mentioned date, she was stopped by Mete, Kadri, Avni Krasniqi from Vranoc village, Peje municipality and Vesel Dizdari from Zllapek village in the presence of the witnesses Hamdi Balaj and Hazir Balaj."

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters kindly ask the Bench to ask the witness to wait for the entire question before answering, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Balaj, could I ask you not to start answering the question until you've heard the whole of the question. You frequently put a response to only half a question, and that's very difficult for the interpreters because then people are speaking at the same time. So please first wait until Mr. Guy-Smith has finished his question and then please respond. MR. DI FAZIO: Your Honours, could I just --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Just --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Just -- MR. DI FAZIO: Just a minor clarification. What statement is being referred to here so we can follow this evidence?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: This is the statement received from the Prosecution, the -- I have a number, R0629065. MR. DI FAZIO: Thanks. But if it could just be identified with a date and -- and --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I did at the beginning. It's the 28th of September, 2002. MR. DI FAZIO: Thanks. Is that an UNMIK statement?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Correct. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: You also said at that time, in 2002: "From the part of Cufe Krasniqi, she was released and she headed alone towards Kodradiqi village at her nephew's."

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: Kodradiqi.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you for the correction. "Avni, Kadri Krasniqi, together with Idriz Gashi, stopped her again and they've taken her to the forest of Vranoc village at the hill called Lug e Shabanit [phoen] and they executed her there."

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: It was Lugu i Isufit, not of Shabanit, that's a mistake. And it was Ibra and Avni who took her in a kind of friendly way. At least, this is what Cufe said. I don't know. I wasn't there.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. My question now is this, sir: You go on to say, "Due to what we find out, she remained there buried for two days, and after that Hysen Ukaj and Ahmet Ukaj from Vranoc e Vogel village, under the pressure of Idriz Gashi and Avni Krasniqi exhumed her. Until now we don't know anything about the place where she was buried and where her bones are." Correct?

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: I mentioned that, and this is how it was. They were two witnesses, Ahmet and Hysen Ukaj. This was mentioned in the trial of 17 of May in Peje. Ahmet Ukaj, together with Durim Hasanaj, a young boy who happened to see two soldiers, but he didn't mention the names, who went to Lugu i Isufit in a red Golf II.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Sir, you had another meeting with UNMIK, and that was on the 2nd of October, 2002.

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And when you met with them at that time, you told them the following: "According to the investigation that I have conducted, these persons killed my sister." And the persons that you are referring to were Mete, Avni, and Idriz Gashi. You go on to say: "And somewhere on the 15th of August, they were -- they buried her. They dug the grave again. Idriz Gashi, Avri -- that's Avni Vranoci --

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: [Not interpreted]: Krasniqi.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: -- Krasniqi on the 15th of August, while using two other persons, named, Hysen Ukaj and Ahmet Ukaj from the village Vranoc, and it is not known where they have taken the body." Correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith, it's now the second time that you put a question in a similar way. You are putting a quote to the witness and then you ask "correct."

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What he stated at the time or --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I'll make it clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: That's what you stated at the time. That's what you told the people at UNMIK at the time, that based upon your investigations, those were the four people who were involved in moving your sister's body; correct?

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: That's correct. At the time, I didn't know Galani. I knew Mete Krasniqi, Iber and Avni, who stopped my sister, and I asked them to tell me where she was. But in order to lay the blame on others, they mentioned others. I didn't know Galani or the others, but I knew the others who collaborated with them, who were together. For a long or for a short time, I don't know. I wasn't interested in pursuing that further. And today they have testified to that, to the court in Peje.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I understand. On the 15th of October, 2002, you spoke with members of the Office of the Prosecutor. You spoke with an investigator by the name of Ole Lehtinen, and at that time, after telling him what happened during the trial where the imam was present, you said the following: "After this, the rumours continued to be heard and one was that a woman was buried in the mountains of Vranoc in a place called Lugu i Isufit near a well. I went there with a few friends of mine and we found a place where the ground had been dug and around I found papers that I knew belonged to Sanije. I dug in the ground, but it was obvious that the body wasn't there any more. I totally lost control and left the place. On my way down from the mountains, I met a young shepherd who saw that I was upset, and he asked me what the matter was. I told him that my sister had been killed there. The boy told me that there had been a body buried in that place. He had seen Avni Krasniqi, Commander Galani, which I know is the nickname of Idriz Gashi, force two soldiers to remove the body from the ground and it was then driven away in a four-by-four vehicle. Avni and Galani had threatened the two soldiers and said they had to vanish the body. I don't know the name of the shepherd. I was so upset at the time. I guess he was approximately 13 or 14 years of age. The shepherd told me that the two forced soldiers were from the village Vranoc and their family name was Ukaj. When you made that statement to the Office of the Prosecutor in October of 2002, that was true, wasn't it? That's what you told them.

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: That was true. And they have come out openly in the court. Even the young boy, Durim Hasanaj. He was eight years old at the time. Now he's 16. They have testified before the court in Peje. They had told this to the Prosecutor as well. They narrated things as they happened. They were four witness. There was someone with Idriz Gashi. They also said that the young boy was taking care of his cattle, he was very upset, that he left, went to his home in Vranoc e Vogel, told his mother what he saw, and that when his father came, Zymer Hasanaj, his wife told him --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Earlier you testified that you were told by some people in 2002. And you said the following: "When I was asked, some people in the court showed me information about him. They said, 'He killed your sister.' I said, 'no, Togeri didn't kill my sister'. And that was all. And what I'd like to ask you --

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: Yes, this is what I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: What I'd like to ask you is: When you were referring to people in the court, were you referring to the trial in 2002 involving Idriz Balaj when you saw him and people said that he killed your sister?

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: I have stated that all the time when they asked me. Whoever from the Prosecutor's asked me, I have said that Idriz Balaj didn't kill my sister. I have found the perpetrator, but they have cast mud at Idriz Balaj. That is, Avni Krasniqi and Iber Krasniqi. I have never said that Idriz Balaj did that, in none of my statements, even in the recent one in Prishtine, when they questioned me. When they asked me whether he killed your sister, I said no. When the process against Idriz Gashi was still underway, they mentioned that. But I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: When you say "they mentioned that," and you're talking about the Prosecutors, when you spoke with the Prosecutors here today, did they discuss with you and ask you whether or not Togeri or Idriz Balaj had killed your sister?

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: They asked me, and I said no, he hasn't but Mete and Avni said this. They have accused him, not me. In none of my statements have I accused Idriz Balaj of having killed my sister. They have accused him of eliminating the body of. But I have not done that. But Avni Krasniqi is still alive. He can be asked about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And when you say, "they have accused him of eliminating the body," my question to you is: When you were speaking with the Prosecution today, did the Prosecution suggest to you that it was Idriz Balaj who had moved the body?

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: They didn't suggest it to me. I simply stated that I forgot to mention that in my statement. And you have the statement even now by Avni Krasniqi in Peje, who, like Mete Krasniqi, who accused him of moving the body. I don't know anything about that. They know. They can -- they should be asked.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... In 2002 on three separate occasions, twice speaking with people from UNMIK and once speaking with a representative from the Office of the Prosecutor, you never mentioned this particular piece of information, that Mete Krasniqi or anyone else had suggested that Idriz Balaj had moved your sister's body, did you?

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: I didn't. It was Mete Krasniqi who suggested that and his brother on 17 May 2007 in his statement in Peje, but not me. I never accused Idriz Balaj. It was he who has accused him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Balaj, the question -- I think you might have understood the issue. When you say that Mete Krasniqi accused - so not yourself but he accused - Idriz Balaj of being involved in removing the body, Mr. Guy-Smith would like to know why you didn't state that in 2002, why you didn't mention it at that time when you gave statements to UNMIK.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It didn't occur to me. I was very upset.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Has any information that you received from Mete Krasniqi concerning your sister's disappearance been true?

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: I don't know whether it was true. When he did what he did to me, sending me to Gllogjan for no reason at all; he might have done anything. But I don't know. I said what he said. And his brother said the same, Avni Krasniqi, and he has his statement. Either in Peje or in here. I don't know. But they said so. I accused them and they accuse someone else. So let them face each other with their accusations and be brought before justice. I didn't accuse anyone. Last time I was in Prishtine, I didn't accuse anyone. When the Prosecutor asked me whether he was involved in the murder of your sister I said no, about Togeri, I mean. I never saw him. I wasn't interested at all in who he was, what he did.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Mr. Balaj, I want to thank you for your time, and I offer you my condolences for your loss.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Harvey.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: No questions.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Balaj, I have a few questions for you, matters which I'd like to seek clarification. Questioned by the Court:

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: In the beginning of your testimony, you explained that Sanije was to buy foodstuffs for the families. And you gave that answer in response to a question which was whether she ever was a member of the KLA as far as you were aware. Do I have to understand your answer that she bought foodstuffs when serving as a member of the KLA?

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: She was not a member of the KLA. She wanted to wear that uniform, and I gave her my rifle. I bought it with my own money in Albania. But she wanted so much to wear the uniform, I gave her the gun. And then when she went to Malisheve, she saw that group of young women. She joined them when they sang the national anthem, the anthem of the KLA together with that group of girls. I did not see that video. I heard that it was recorded. But at that time, she was wearing my uniform and had my gun. At that time, she went to buy food for people in the village, not for the KLA. Things like cigarettes. Mostly cigarettes, as a matter of fact. And other things that she could buy with the money that the people had given her. Because they knew that she was traveling to Baran, to Malisheve, and they knew that Sanije had money and that we were a good family and they asked her to bring things back for them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: We worked. Our family has worked abroad, in Germany, other countries, so we have money.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So I also do understand from your answer that when you provided her with a uniform or with a weapon, that that was not because you held any position in the KLA. Or did I misunderstand your testimony in this respect?

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: No, I did not have a position. I was a simple soldier. I wanted to protect my home. I was an honest person in my village. I was an honest person to everybody, my brothers and my whole clan, 30 Balaj households. I just gave her the uniform to wear. Why not? I brought it from Albania. I went through lots of things. I could have been killed when I went there and came back. I could have been killed by the Serbs. And I think it was my right to give her my uniform if I wanted to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Was that a KLA uniform or a uniform with any KLA patches on it or ...

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: It was a uniform of the Albanian army. It was a camouflage uniform, various colours, green and other colours, and a cap. I think the cap had the KLA patch on. And also, there was a patch of the KLA on the arm sleeve and on the chest. The cap resembled the caps that are kept now by -- that are worn now by our police.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. When I earlier asked you whether you had any position in the KLA under which you provided her with a uniform and a weapon, of course I meant to say that you -- whether you had -- or I meant to ask you whether you had any position in which you were competent to distribute uniforms or weapons, because I do understand from, especially the statement that you gave, that you were involved in getting arms from Albania. Is that correctly understood?

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: Yes. I went to Albania to get arms, and I tried to make my contribution. I put the life of myself and my family in danger. I just wanted to protect -- to defend Kosova, a soldier who defended his own family and his own country, the life of any person who lived in Kosova. I got the uniform. That was my uniform and I gave it to her to wear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And do I also then understand you correctly if this implies that she was never under any orders by a superior in the KLA?

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: No, she was not under any orders. She was staying at home. I had people at home, about 50 people of the Selmani family, who were staying with me for six months, and she helped them. She stayed with this family, with our family, took care of them. And whenever I was not home, she was the one who protected everybody. Because I could have been killed when I went to help the KLA, to assist whenever fighting was occurring. She was the one who took care of all the children. At that time, they were very young.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Then one other matter where I'd like to seek clarification. You said - and I read from the transcript - "He knew" - and you were talking then about Din Krasniqi - "He knew that he worked with Galani." And he was referring to his brother Mete Krasniqi. "He himself worked with Galani with his brothers. They were military police. They were commanders. They referred to each other by the name of 'commander'". Could you be very precise in your answer: Who exactly called whom "commander"?

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: Well, as I said earlier, everybody was a commander. Din Krasniqi was appointed, I think, commander. His village elected him as a leader or commander of the village. But as for the other ones, nobody appointed them, nobody elected them, nobody commanded them. I will always say this. I've mentioned this before. I will say it again. If they had been under the command of Tahir Zemaj, Nazif Ramabaja, or Ramush, they would not have allowed these people to do what they did. Ramush would not have allowed them. Tahir Zemaj would not have allowed them. And Nazif Ramabaja, the same. They would not have allowed them to do the things they did to my sister.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You also said in this respect: "They were military police." Who did you refer to exactly when you said "they were military police"?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honours, just so I have some clarification. Are we just discussing his testimony or are we talking about --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's page 55, line -- "he himself worked with Galani with his brothers. They were military police," it reads on line 10.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could you please tell us exactly to whom you referred when you said "they were military police. They were commanders." And why you understood them to be military police.

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: Well, they called themselves military police, because the real military police did not do the stupid things that they did. The military police behaved properly towards people.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then you're referring to Mete Krasniqi again or whom else?

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: Well, Mete, Avni, Iber, these people who were involved in stopping and killing my -- my sister, in collaboration with Galani. I didn't know about Galani. I saw a photograph of him in Peje, in black clothes together with Mete Krasniqi and Vesel Dizdari. They were also wearing black clothes. That's when I saw them in black clothes. When I met Mete myself, he was wearing civilian clothes the first time I went to see him. I was so angry and upset, I didn't even pay attention to the clothes, but when I saw the photograph in the courtroom, the photograph that was shown to the judge and the prosecutor and defence attorney, I saw Mete Krasniqi wearing a black uniform, Vesel Dizdari in black uniform, and Galani, Idriz Gashi, in black uniform. That was when I saw them. Well, they could have worn all kinds of uniforms, black or camouflage, and so on. We had people in our village who had black uniforms but were not members of the military police.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for that answer. One second, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you take off your earphones for a second. Do you understand any English?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You do understand English? No -- Mr. Di Fazio. MR. DI FAZIO: I don't believe he does.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I would like to raise the following issue: We allowed the witness to show a few photographs of a funeral. The coffin or the body was covered by a red flag with a black eagle on it. The Chamber, although did not seek to obtain this information for purposes of evidence, but nevertheless not everyone is buried covered by a flag. The Chamber would like to give an opportunity to the parties, if they consider it of any relevance, to put questions to it and gives notice that this is what the Chamber observed, for full transparency of our observations. I don't know whether you want to seek any further clarification. The Chamber might ask a question on it itself, but at the same time it would not do so unless it had given an opportunity to the parties to consider putting a question on that matter. No, I see from the Defence side there seems to be no ... Mr. Di Fazio. MR. DI FAZIO: Would Your Honours just give me a moment, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: MR. DI FAZIO: I'll just ask a few questions, if I can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please do so. Could you please put on your earphones again. And may I ask you to introduce the matter in a -- such a gentle way, because it's a very emotional issue and -- MR. DI FAZIO: I understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And I can imagine that one would ask about what the habit is or about -- seek in a very cautious way. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes. Yes, yes. Further examination by Mr. Di Fazio:

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Witness, Mr. Balaj, you showed us earlier some photographs - four, I think, in total - of your late sister's funeral earlier this year, I believe. I wonder if you still have them. Could I -- could I see them again, please.

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The first and/or the third, not the second and the fourth. MR. DI FAZIO: Well, I can't remember the sequence, but I think I know which one is -- oh, yes. Okay. Could the usher hand these two back to the witness, these two. And that can also go -- the other two can be put away.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Now, just the two photos that I'm showing you there show a -- a portion of your sister's funeral. And you see a -- a flag there. How -- how and why was that flag placed -- placed there?

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: This is our national flag. We use it. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you. Questioned by the Court:

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Do I understand you that it's customary to use the national flag at burials to cover the body of civilians in general terms or ...

utterances.speaker: SHABAN BALAJ
utterances.text: No. People who were killed during the war are buried with this flag. People who die a natural death do not have this flag upon their coffin. This flag came from the morgue, as a matter of fact, where my sister was kept, in Rahovec. We did not put that flag on the coffin. It came from the morgue like that where my sister was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much for that answer. Is there any further need to put questions to the witness? If not -- Mr. Balaj, this concludes your testimony. Of course, the Chamber has noticed that it took you back to emotional events. The Chamber would like to thank you for coming to The Hague and to answer questions of both parties and of the Bench. We wish you a safe trip home again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Your Honours. You know things about justice. You are judging this case. And you will bring the truth out. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, would you please escort the witness out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber was informed that the next witness scheduled who had some medical problems today is ready to appear at quarter past 6.00 in this courtroom. That's the latest information which -- at 5.31 we were informed that the witness was still under medical care. At 5.36 we were informed that he could be here at quarter past 6.00. I take it that proper attention will be paid to the medical condition, and of course the Chamber will also verify that, but in public it might not be possible to do that in depth, but I take it, Mr. Di Fazio, that proper attention will be paid to the witness who, if for medical reasons is not able to testify, does not enter the court. But we, for -- on the basis of this information, we'll have a break and -- Yes, Mr. Di Fazio. MR. DI FAZIO: I'm not entirely sure I've understood correctly. Do you -- are Your Honours inviting the Prosecution to -- to make sure that the witness is able and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well -- MR. DI FAZIO: Able in all the circumstances to start tonight?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I read at 5.31 that - and I'm now paraphrasing - as far as the Prosecution knows, he is still in hospital. If then five minutes later I receive that we were informed that the witness can be here at quarter past 6.00 to start his testimony, the only thing I'm saying is that under those circumstances, of course, it -- it's important to verify just for yourself that the witness you call is in a position and is in a medical condition that he's able to testify. I take it that this information does not only say that he can be in the courtroom in half an hour but also that his condition is such that it is acceptable that he appears. MR. DI FAZIO: We'll -- I'll make sure that all of those inquiries are attended to. If -- if for any reason we have misgivings about his ability to start today or to testify today, I'll make sure that everyone's notified immediately.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then we'll have a break. I take it that there are --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: No, that's perfectly all right. Mr. Di Fazio and I spoke about this early this afternoon, and I had suggested that if -- that if there was any undue strain upon anybody --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: -- who was suffering from a medical condition that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The information the Chamber received -- well, let's say on the basis of very general knowledge of medical matters, would not indicate necessarily that the witness could in such condition not testify and at the same time it is a condition where some additional caution is rightly placed.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you for the general information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We adjourn until quarter past 6.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could -- before we -- yes. Please put on the earphones. Please sit down for a second, Mr. Hasanaj. I'd like to turn into private session for a moment.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hasanaj, before you give evidence in this court, the Rules of Procedure and Evidence require you to make a solemn declaration that you'll speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth. May I invite you to stand. The text of the solemn declaration will be handed out to you by Mr. Usher. May invite you to make that solemn declaration. Mr. Usher, could you please give the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Hasanaj. Please be seated. You'll first be examined by Mr. Re, who's counsel for the Prosecution. Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Good evening, Mr. Hasanaj.

utterances.speaker: ZYMER HASANAJ
utterances.text: Good evening.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you some questions and I'm going to show you some statement and one map -- or sorry, two maps. Firstly, your name is Zymer Hasanaj? Have I pronounced that correctly?

utterances.speaker: ZYMER HASANAJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And your date of birth is the 16th of June, 1952?

utterances.speaker: ZYMER HASANAJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You were born in Vranoc e Vogel in Deqan?

utterances.speaker: ZYMER HASANAJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And you're a Kosovar Albanian.

utterances.speaker: ZYMER HASANAJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What is your occupation now?

utterances.speaker: ZYMER HASANAJ
utterances.text: Now I work as a taxi driver.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Where is that?

utterances.speaker: ZYMER HASANAJ
utterances.text: In Deqan.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Now, I'm going to show you a statement, which is in English and Albanian. And it -- you signed it today, and I'm going to ask you some questions about that statement. Can the witness please be shown the hard copy, which is 65 ter exhibit 2068, and it has an annexed map which is referred to as Annex A. I'm not sure whether the Defence have actually received the annex, which is the map which has got the "X's the witness has marked on of certain villages. Am I correct in that?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I think we have it attached to an earlier statement, not to the 92 ter.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can you please look at the statement, Mr. Hasanaj. All right. Is that the statement you signed this morning, Mr. Hasanaj?

utterances.speaker: ZYMER HASANAJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And does it accurately reflect -- is it accurate? Does it accurately reflect your signature in the declaration there?

utterances.speaker: ZYMER HASANAJ
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And does it say what you would tell the Judges if you were asked to give -- if you were asked to tell them what's in that statement? Is it what you would say if I or the Judges or any of the lawyers here asked you the same questions?

utterances.speaker: ZYMER HASANAJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: On that basis, may it please be received into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, could you please assign a number to the statement.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That's P923, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Are there any objections against the ...? Then it's admitted into evidence. I add to that the following: Mr. Re, you asked for the identity of this witness. With the previous witness, that was not done. I have understood the identity of the previous witness to be established on the basis of his confirmation that he signed the first page of his statement; although, he was not specifically asked whether he was the person whose name appears on that document. If the Defence would think of it in any different way, I'd like to know it now rather than when the witness has returned. Mr. Re, this was -- as a matter of fact, was an excursion to the previous witness, rather than -- it had nothing to do with the present witness. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I just want to ask you a few clarifying questions based upon what is written in the statement which you have in your hand there. Now, could you please go to paragraph 2 in which -- oh, I'm sorry. Might I read onto the record the one-page summary which I have prepared --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Perhaps -- is the witness aware of -- of how it works? Then -- otherwise, I'll explain to him briefly what we are going to do now.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I'm more than happy for Your Honour to do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Hasanaj, since there's no need for you to repeat all the answers you've given already and which are put on paper, but for the public to know what your testimony is about, Mr. Re will read a short summary of what we find in your statement so that the public is aware of your evidence as well. So just listen, and then later on Mr. Re will have some further questions for you. Mr. Re, has the Defence received a copy of the summary? No objections. Then please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The witness is from Vranoc e Vogel in Deqan. From March 1998 his village and seven or eight around it started organising it -- sorry, started organising to monitor the situation. They considered themselves to be KLA and obtained weapons and military attire with KLA insignia. Sometime after a Serb attack on the 29th of May, 1998, the villagers were sent via Gllogjan to obtain weapons from Albania.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Re, let me just -- you're hesitating, and I can imagine a reason why.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I was just waiting for the French to catch up with me, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Oh, that's good.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And they did eventually.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Ramush Haradinaj came to Vranoc on many occasions. In mid-April 1998, he came to announce the appointment of Din Krasniqi as the commander of the Lugu i Baran regions, which included about 25 villages, including Vranoc. People -- people accepted the expression "God in heaven, Ramush on earth," meaning that he had great authority. Serb forces attacked on the 29th of May, 1998. They withdrew from the village at about 6.00 p.m. That night. Serb forces also attacked Prilep, Carabreg, and Strellc that day. A "free zone" came into operation in the Dukagjini valley by the end of March 1998 and except for occasions such as the 29th of May, the witness -- such as the offensive on the 29th of May, the witness could travel between Vranoc and Gllogjan without coming across a Serb soldier or police officer. The witness went to Gllogjan to see Ramush Haradinaj after the attack of 29th of May to obtain assistance. Ramush Haradinaj subsequently came to Vranoc to see whether they had sufficient supplies. On the day that Sanije Balaj was killed in August 1998, the witness's eight-year-old son told him that he and two friends had been near a water spring at Lugu i Isufit and had seen two men forcing a woman out of a car. The men yelled at the boys to leave. They did and heard three gunshots. The witness went with his son to the place and also with Ahmet Ukaj and Hysen Ukaj. They went to the place. When they were there, a person called to them to stop and they saw a man crouching wearing a cap with a KLA symbol. Ahmet Ukaj later told him that Idriz Gashi and Avni Krasniqi were there. Ahmet Ukaj -- Ahmet Ukaj told him that Galani had killed a woman there and that Galani had threatened him - that is, Ukaj - not to tell anyone. The witness reported the incident to Din Krasniqi, the commander in the area, that night and told him to go and report it to the commander in Baran, Nazif Ramabaja. Okay. That -- that completes the summary which is contained -- what is contained in the 92 ter summary -- sorry, statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Re, I have paragraph -- yes. I have at this moment on my screen paragraph 15. I do not know what the reason for that is, but I noticed that in the English language that we certainly find a third person giving a statement. If you look at the second line of paragraph 15, it reads not but "I do not know anything," but it reads "he does not know anything," which is quite extraordinary in the statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is that correct in the original or is it a translation error or is it -- or are you refer -- or is the witness referring there to Toger, which would come as a surprise, to say the least?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: No, it's just a simple error.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: A simple error. Okay. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: It's been corrected when the statement was taken. I think someone wrote in "he does," referring to the witness does not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: It's been corrected. The version which has been put into e-court should have "I do not know anything about their activities" and the witness's corrected signature next to it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The Chamber has no access to upload the documents in e-court and has to deal with the hard copies that are provided before to the Chamber. So if that's corrected, then that's resolved. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can you please go to paragraph 2 of your statement, Mr. Hasanaj. And in your statement, you refer to considering yourselves to be KLA but did not have a commander as such. My question is: Why did you consider yourselves to be KLA?

utterances.speaker: ZYMER HASANAJ
utterances.text: As a KLA member and representative of Vranoc e Vogel, which is a small village, actually, I was responsible more for emergency issues, like food supplies, surveying the terrain lest some attacks might be launched, and we should in that case evacuate the people.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Was there a -- how did you formally come to be in the KLA?

utterances.speaker: ZYMER HASANAJ
utterances.text: I came to be a member of the KLA when Lugu i Baranit was part of Peje commune. Being near Vranoc when Vranoc e Vogel was attacked, after Gllogjan was attacked we didn't feel safe in our village. We were afraid of other attacks. After that we were sitting in a room and seeing whether Serbs -- Serb forces would be coming or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: When was it that you formally became part of the KLA?

utterances.speaker: ZYMER HASANAJ
utterances.text: I don't remember the exact date. I know that it was sometime in the middle of April. And I take pride in the fact that I was a member of the KLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Was there a commander of the people who considered themselves to be KLA in April 1998 in your village?

utterances.speaker: ZYMER HASANAJ
utterances.text: We didn't have any commander at that time, but as a person who was in a position to contact people, to be kind of representative, I would say. This is how it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: In paragraph 4, you refer to Ramush Haradinaj coming to Vranoc on many occasions, including to announce the appointment of Din Krasniqi as the commander of the Lugu i Baran region. Did you know Ramush Haradinaj personally?

utterances.speaker: ZYMER HASANAJ
utterances.text: I do know Ramush Haradinaj personally. After the offensive against Vranoc, Ramush Haradinaj didn't appoint Din Krasniqi. It was the people who elected him. And it was after the Gllogjan offensive that he became known, Ramush Haradinaj, offensive during which there were many casualties.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can you give us a date of this Gllogjan offensive?

utterances.speaker: ZYMER HASANAJ
utterances.text: I am not certain of the date, but in Deqan commune it was during the first offensive. At least, this is how we know it, when the they attacked Gllogjan.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Was that before the Serb offensive of the 29th of -- or the Serb attack on your village of the 29th of May?

utterances.speaker: ZYMER HASANAJ
utterances.text: On the 29th of May, they attacked us at 5.00 in the morning. The Vranoc village was attacked by the Serb forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What I'm asking you is about -- did Ramush Haradinaj become known before then? And if so, how far? How long before then?

utterances.speaker: ZYMER HASANAJ
utterances.text: Before the Gllogjan offensive, he was not known, Ramush Haradinaj; at least, I didn't know him either personally or even by name.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Just so we know what you're talking -- everyone knows -- understands what you mean by "the Gllogjan offensive," can you describe to the Trial Chamber what you're referring to. I mean, what happened in the Gllogjan offensive?

utterances.speaker: ZYMER HASANAJ
utterances.text: From what I heard - because I wasn't there, present - during this Gllogjan offensive, the village was attacked. Everybody heard that there were numerous forces. Three people were killed on that day. The others fled to other villages. I don't know where. It is based only on hearsay, because I wasn't there to see it with my own eyes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: In paragraph 5, you refer to an expression: "God in heaven; Ramush on earth," meaning that he had great authority. Then you say: "No one was superior to him." I just want you to tell the Trial Chamber, the Judges, what you mean by "no one was superior to" Ramush.

utterances.speaker: ZYMER HASANAJ
utterances.text: I -- I said this because from -- every time there was a Serb attack until the KLA became engaged in the war, when the name became known, Ramush -- that of Ramush Haradinaj, it was myself who put that expression, "God in heaven; Ramush on earth."

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What do you mean by "no one was superior to him"?

utterances.speaker: ZYMER HASANAJ
utterances.text: I thought that -- how can you put up resistance to the enemy. I didn't know that it was difficult to put up resistance. In fact, it was very small resistance that was put up.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I'm not sure I quite understand your answer. I'm asking you about why you say that no one was superior to him. What do you mean by "superior to" Ramush?

utterances.speaker: ZYMER HASANAJ
utterances.text: After he -- he became known -- I don't know how it has been translated there, but I personally gave this description. It was my personal opinion.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And what I'm -- what do you mean by it? That's what I'm asking: What do you mean by "no one was superior to him"?

utterances.speaker: ZYMER HASANAJ
utterances.text: He was good then and he's good now -- I mean, he's loved by people. He's considered -- he is -- he's held in esteem by the Albanian people. If you allow me, I would like to continue. There is a wise saying: "The children eat the fruit in the trees and the parents get sore teeth".

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's explanation. It might mean to say that the parents suffered for the deeds of the children.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Okay. Same paragraph, you refer to Ramush always acting as a simple soldier. Then you said: "He assumed the front position with everyone sitting around him in a circle." What do you mean by assuming the front position with everyone sitting around him in a circle? Describe to the Trial Chamber what you mean.

utterances.speaker: ZYMER HASANAJ
utterances.text: According to the Albanian customs and traditions, everyone who comes from outside the village is given priority in the seating.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Describe the intensity of the attack on the 29th of May on your village by the Serb forces and the response by the KLA.

utterances.speaker: ZYMER HASANAJ
utterances.text: On 29th of May at 5.00 in the morning, we heard shots. They had come and taken positions on a hill -- they had come with infantry troops and started shooting. That day Vranoc e Madh -- during that time, there was only one guard that kept guard duty, and that guard missed the forces, didn't see the forces come. So then after that, they brought heavy artillery and we couldn't respond to their fire. When they came with tanks and APCs and other heavy war machinery, the village, Vranoc e Vogel, could be an easy target for the forces. There was a forest nearby. Upon the first shots, people started to leave their houses and go to other villages, Maznik, Lumbardh, Dashinoc, and some other villages, those who could make it. Some were burnt, were carbonised. Three people, actually. One was killed by the tank fire. Near Lugu i Isufit, one person. Imer Ukaj was his name.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: How many were on the Serb side and how many were on the KLA in the -- the conflict that day? I mean approximately.

utterances.speaker: ZYMER HASANAJ
utterances.text: On the Serb side, we couldn't count them. We only saw that they had a lot of artillery means; whereas, we, we were very few in numbers. We couldn't do anything. We couldn't resist them.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Why did the Serbs withdraw at about 6.00 that night?

utterances.speaker: ZYMER HASANAJ
utterances.text: I don't know the reason why. They set fire to the village. More than half the houses of the village. They killed some, as I said. They killed livestock. They destroyed everything they could. As I said, four persons were burned.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: In your statement in paragraph 15, you refer to Idriz Balaj and Toger as one and the same person. Did you know Idriz Balaj, Toger, in 1998?

utterances.speaker: ZYMER HASANAJ
utterances.text: No. No. I didn't know him.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Do you know whether he came to your village?

utterances.speaker: ZYMER HASANAJ
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown Exhibit P10 in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Now, while this is coming up, I'm going to show you a map and I'm going to ask you to mark on the map the position of the location of Lugu i Isufit. And --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. -- Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you do so, that -- if the witness says that a person is one and the same, although known by two names, and if he then testifies that he doesn't know that person, then would it not be a good idea to establish the basis on which he comes to the conclusion that's one and the same person?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: If it assists the Trial Chamber, I'll --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. Otherwise, I wouldn't know how he knows.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Mr. Hasanaj, how do you know that Toger and Idriz Balaj are the same person?

utterances.speaker: ZYMER HASANAJ
utterances.text: People said so, because people at the time went by pseudonyms, and this is how people knew them, by pseudonyms. And I heard even after the war, after he was gaoled the first time, everybody knew who he was. That's why I said that Idriz Balaj and Togeri are one and the same person.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The map is now on the screen. I take it, Mr. Re, you are aware that zooming in and zooming out, once marking starts, there's no further zooming in or zooming out.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: We've got it just where we want it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can you see Vranovac on the map in the top right-hand corner and can you see Dasinovac on the map and can you see Zarki Pojas marked on? About one third of the way down, just slightly to the right of the middle?

utterances.speaker: ZYMER HASANAJ
utterances.text: Between Dashinoc and Vranoc, Vranoc e Vogel.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can you see the place called Lugu i Isufit there?

utterances.speaker: ZYMER HASANAJ
utterances.text: Yes, it is there.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: All right. Do we have a red pen?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And just put a big cross over the top of it, a large cross, please.

utterances.speaker: ZYMER HASANAJ
utterances.text: Here, above this place.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You've actually marked it just below Dasinovac. Is it where Zarki Pojas is, a bit above the road? Or have I got that wrong?

utterances.speaker: ZYMER HASANAJ
utterances.text: I can't find it here.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can you see where Zarki Pojas is?

utterances.speaker: ZYMER HASANAJ
utterances.text: I can't see Zarki Pojas here.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Below Kodradiqi.

utterances.speaker: ZYMER HASANAJ
utterances.text: Unless it's here. I can't see it very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Just go up above where you put your red cross. You might see it.

utterances.speaker: ZYMER HASANAJ
utterances.text: Unless it's here. I can't see it very well. It is between Dashinoc and Vranovc. It was a cooperative field but it was otherwise called Zarki Pojas. This is where Lugu i Isufit is.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Okay. If you look at Zarki Pojas it's directly underneath --

utterances.speaker: ZYMER HASANAJ
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. I apologise. I've found it. Yes, where the two "Z"s are, is the place called Lugu i Isufit. Here, can I draw it?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can we refresh it, please, so he can redo it, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I do understand that it is a way of getting rid of some of the markings. I don't know whether that would affect all the markings or whether you could choose.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: If we could just wipe it and he could put the second "X," the one above it again, I think it would make the record --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. If we could -- perhaps we could have the original unmarked document again on the screen. Yes. Yes. Could you now, please, indicate the place where you --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Thank you. May that please be received into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Registrar, that would be exhibit number...?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: P924, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If there is no objection, it is admitted into evidence. Mr. Re, I'm looking at the clock. I think we'll have to -- to finish for the day.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I suspect I've finished, but I'll let you know in the morning. I think I've finished as much as I need to go.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Just one second, please. Mr. Hasanaj, we'll finish for the day. We'd like to see you back tomorrow at quarter past 2.00 in this same courtroom. You'll then be further examined. I have one matter I'm drawing the attention of the -- First of all, Mr. Re, I stand corrected. I received half an hour before the -- before we started at quarter past 6.00, I received the latest version of the 92 ter statement, so -- and that was already the corrected one. So I stand corrected when I said that the Chamber had not received it. I was wondering what the saying in the language actually meant, whether it is that parents are suffering under the acts of the children. I also could imagine that it is that those who are in charge are carrying the burden of what others enjoy and that could be for leaders and people, parents and children. I'm just wondering if anyone would be in a position to -- or perhaps with the assistance of the interpreters, to find the correct meaning of the saying the witness expressed, then that would certainly assist the Chamber. We adjourn until quarter past 2.00, 2nd of October, Courtroom I.
